title: ProviderConfiguration
description: Shape of the stored model-provider configuration and its role assignments, for agent/contracts/provider-configuration@0.1.0. The user brings their own provider and pays their own bill, so this document describes a provider, refers to a credential without carrying it, and binds each role to a model. It is displayed, exported for inspection and replicated to the account, which is why no member of it may hold a secret value. What the file cannot express is stated by the contract document: that every role resolves, falling back to the provider's recommended default rather than creating a job that would fail on its first call, and that cost figures are display only and never a gate.

providers.description: The configured providers. A provider is a place calls are sent and a credential reference, never a credential.

id.description: Stable identity of this provider within the configuration; role assignments refer to it.

kind.description: How the provider is reached and paid for. A custom provider is the only kind that carries its own base address.

credentialRef.description: A reference into the operating system's secure storage. The credential exists in exactly one place and every other entity holds a reference, which is what lets this document be displayed, exported and replicated.

baseUrl.description: Present only for a custom provider.

inputs.description: The declared input capability, read before a call is attempted. The composer disables image attachment when the model assigned to the role that would receive the image declares no image input, because sending an image to a model that cannot accept it is a failure the user cannot see.

costPerMillionInput.description: Display only. Never a gate: the account and the bill are the user's own.

costPerMillionOutput.description: Display only, on the same footing as the input figure.

assignments.description: Which model each role runs under. A role with no entry here resolves to the provider's recommended default rather than to nothing.

role.description: The five roles the product runs. Adding one is a MINOR change; removing one or changing what it means is MAJOR.

source.description: Distinguishes a recommended default from the user's own choice, so a later release may change the recommendation without overwriting a deliberate decision.
